measurement_notes: Single-motor phase voltages refer to conditioned PWM phase-node measurements as in the saved inverter; no sinusoidal post-filter output is implied.
Boost input voltage example is rectified input; confirm the actual sensing point when the topology is selected.
Vienna upper/lower half-bus inputs are conditioned voltage measurements of the two bus-capacitor sections; do not tie the physical bus midpoint to controller GND just to obtain these measurements.
All ports receive low-voltage, reference-compatible conditioned signals. An NTC role needs a divider/excitation front end; it does not mean wiring a raw NTC directly across a signal/GND ADC port.

power_control_interface.PWM_ports_contain: PWM and GND only; no raw power, ADC, ENABLE, FAULT or READY signals inside the 8P ports.
power_control_interface.separate_CTRL_ports: Proposed A/B 6P each: ENABLE, FAULT_N, BASE_READY, CTRL_READY, BRAKE and GND. Physical pin order pending. CTRL_READY is the shared reset-qualified ARM output, not an extra GPIO; BRAKE_B remains a reserved pin, not an implemented second brake circuit.
power_control_interface.startup: Both boards require default-disabled hardware gating independent of MCU boot output levels. CTRL_READY = CORE_RESET_OK AND RUN_ARM; each board also requires its own ENABLE and local hardware-OK.
power_control_interface.ROM_loader: AN2606 G431 Table116 lists PC10/PC11 as ROM USART3 TX/RX and PC8 as I2C3 SCL: all overlap PWM_B. BOOT/ROM must not obtain ARM permission; hardware gating must suppress any ROM-level activity. PD5/PD6 have USART2 alternate functions, but that ROM table selects PA2/PA3, not PD5/PD6; do not infer ROM use from an AF entry alone.
power_control_interface.fault: Each local power board closes its own hardware protection path and reports FAULT_N to the corresponding advanced-timer BKIN. Do not replace hardware cutoff with software polling.
power_control_interface.brake: TIM15 is separate from TIM1/TIM8 and remains available after bridge fault. Brake startup permission must use reset/ARM; bridge FAULT must not automatically suppress required braking.
power_control_interface.electrical: 3.3V logic and conditioned ADC voltages. Gate drivers, high-voltage sensing and any required isolation remain power-board responsibilities. Mains-version isolation is not decided by this pin plan.

firmware_constraints: Each PWM port is three complementary pairs, not six arbitrary independently timed PWM outputs; port A and port B use separate advanced timers.

TIM1/TIM8 PWM frequency, ADC trigger/sequence and CPU budget must be designed for the selected motor OR PFC application; they do not run together on this controller. Two 20kHz FOC loops plus ThreadX are not validated here.
Two ADC instances remain shared; physical analog pin reservations do not increase simultaneous ADC capacity.
ABZ uses independent TIM2/TIM4 encoder counters; Z inputs are GPIO interrupts, not promised hardware timer-index reset.
SPI_A and SPI_B remain independent hardware SPI1/SPI3 buses; release PB3/PB4 JTAG/SWO while retaining PA13/PA14 SWD.

I2C1 and I2C2 are separate open-drain buses, each with a separately sized 3.3V pullup network. Disable unused UCPD dead-battery pulls affecting PB6 and PA9 before encoder/I2C use; verify option bytes for PB8 BOOT0 and PG10 NRST.
Keep PE2-PE5 trace functions disabled when used for the four GPIO LEDs; power LED uses no GPIO.
CAN keeps current classic-CAN PHY qualification; changing package does not validate CAN-FD operation.
